body.x: Program Director, Training & Capacity Strengthening (Training & Capacity Strengthening Department) [based in Seoul]

We are seeking a Program Director, Training & Capacity Strengthening for a 2-year-regular position to work within Training & Capacity Strengthening Department at the International Vaccine Institute in Seoul, Korea. (Duty station: Seoul, Korea)
Job Description

The incumbent works to provide strategic, technical and operational leadership for IVI’s Training & Capacity Strengthening portfolio within the IDPR Unit. The incumbent develops and delivers sustainable programs that strengthen the capabilities of vaccine and biopharmaceutical professionals, institutions and partner countries across research, development, manufacturing and regulatory practice. Working with IVI teams and external partners, the Director translates workforce needs into practical training, institutional capacity strengthening and measurable improvements in vaccine access and pandemic/outbreak readiness.
Key Roles & Responsibilities
1. Lead TCS strategy and institutional capacity strengthening
Develop and implement a multi-year TCS strategy and annual work plans aligned with IVI’s mission, IDPR priorities and partner-country needs.
Lead workforce and institutional needs assessments with manufacturers, regulators, research institutions and ministries; translate findings into prioritized capacity-strengthening roadmaps.
Integrate training with IVI’s research, technology-transfer, manufacturing and preparedness programs to support sustained institutional capability.
2. Direct technical training and curriculum development

Oversee competency-based curricula and practical training in vaccine and biopharmaceutical development and manufacturing, including cell culture, purification, quality control, quality assurance and GMP principles.
Develop training for regulatory reviewers and industry professionals on manufacturing processes, product quality and regulatory science, with appropriate subject-matter experts.
Coordinate relevant modules on nonclinical models, efficacy evaluation, research ethics, biosafety and emerging biotechnology; ensure scientific accuracy and relevance to vaccine programs.
3. Ensure program delivery and training quality
Direct classroom, laboratory, facility-based, blended and in-country training; establish learning objectives, participant selection criteria, trainer standards and assessment methods.
Build train-the-trainer programs, mentoring and follow-up support that enable partner institutions to deliver and sustain training locally.
Ensure safe, well-documented delivery with host facilities and technical teams, including appropriate biosafety, participant welfare, confidentiality and intellectual-property arrangements.
4. Build partnerships and mobilize resources
Lead TCS partnerships with government agencies, international organizations, development banks, universities, manufacturers and specialized training institutions.
Advance international training cooperation, including Global Training Hub for Biomanufacturing (GTH-B)activities and related programs, in coordination with IVI colleagues and partners.
Develop technical proposals, budgets and partnership arrangements with business development and other relevant teams; secure grants, sponsored training and other sustainable funding opportunities.
5. Manage people, budgets and program operations
Lead and develop TCS staff, trainers and consultants; set objectives, delegate responsibilities and manage performance within the approved organizational structure.
Oversee budgets, staffing, schedules, training facilities and delivery partners; monitor expenditure, resource utilization, delivery risks and contractual obligations.
Coordinate with Finance, Human Resources, Procurement, Legal and other relevant functions to ensure timely delivery, compliance and sound stewardship of funds.
6. Demonstrate results and represent IVI
Establish indicators for learning attainment, application of skills, institutional adoption, participant reach and cost-effectiveness; use follow-up assessments to evaluate outcomes.
Ensure timely, accurate reporting to IVI leadership, donors and partners; maintain training records, curricula, knowledge resources and lessons learned.
Represent IVI in technical and policy forums, advise the Deputy Director General on workforce development and undertake other relevant duties assigned by the supervisor.
Job Requirements and Qualifications
1. Education Requirements
Master’s degree in biotechnology, pharmaceutical sciences, veterinary medicine, life sciences, public health or a related discipline. A Ph.D. in a relevant scientific field is preferred.
2. Related Field Work Experience

At least 20 years of relevant experience in biopharmaceutical or vaccine training, workforce development, manufacturing, regulatory support or translational research, including at least 5 years leading teams or substantial training programs.
Demonstrated experience managing publicly funded or donor-supported programs, budgets and multidisciplinary partnerships. International capacity-building experience is required.
3. Technical and Professional Skills / Knowledge
Strong knowledge of biopharmaceutical manufacturing processes, GMP principles and quality systems, with experience translating technical content into practical training.
Expertise in training needs assessment, curriculum design, adult learning, competency assessment and training quality assurance.
Understanding of regulatory science and nonclinical development relevant to vaccine and biopharmaceutical capacity strengthening.
Ability to manage complex portfolios, budgets, contracts and delivery risks, and to develop proposals and sustainable partnerships.
Strong negotiation, presentation and stakeholder-management skills, including engagement with senior government, industry and international partners.
Proficiency in digital learning and program-management tools; ability to assess the relevance of AI and emerging biotechnology to workforce development.
4. Key Competency
Strategic leadership; people development; partnership building; results orientation; accountability; communication; cross-cultural collaboration; commitment to continuous learning.
5. Language Proficiency
Professional fluency in spoken and written English is required.
Korean proficiency is desirable for engagement with Korean training institutions, industry and government partners.
